cohort: The study included 198 term neonates, divided into three groups: DCT-positive ABO-incompatible neonates, DCT-negative ABO-incompatible neonates with hyperbilirubinemia, and healthy controls.
finding: Cord blood COHb levels were not superior to the direct Coombs test for predicting the risk of developing severe hyperbilirubinemia in term neonates.
cross-section timing: At birth (cord blood measurements) and early neonatal period (TSB levels).
